edges.description: Reduced NFIA transcriptional regulation is occasionally associated with premature closure of metopic, lambdoid, or sagittal sutures via an unestablished craniofacial osteogenic mechanism.
NFIA dosage insufficiency is associated with variable craniofacial dysmorphism.
Disrupted spinal cord glial and neural development in NFIA haploinsufficiency is associated with tethered spinal cord.
Impaired CNS gliogenesis, neuronal migration, and commissural circuit assembly produce global developmental delay.
Perturbed cortical and midline neuroglial development results in variable intellectual disability.
Central nervous system developmental dysfunction manifests early as generalized hypotonia.
Structural and cellular CNS developmental abnormalities predispose a subset of affected individuals to seizures.
Central nervous system malformation is occasionally accompanied by strabismus.
Congenital ventriculomegaly and hydrocephalus expand cranial volume, contributing directly to progressive macrocephaly.
Altered posterior fossa and intracranial CSF dynamics are accompanied by tonsillar herniation below the foramen magnum.
Craniocervical CSF-flow obstruction and spinal malformation are associated with spinal cord syrinx formation.
Vesicoureteral reflux and urinary stasis predispose affected individuals to ascending pyelonephritis and recurrent urinary tract infections.

nodes.description: Nfia is expressed in the developing ureter and metanephric mesenchyme and is required in a dosage-sensitive manner for ureteral and renal development; its loss produces abnormalities of the ureteropelvic and ureterovesical junctions with vesicoureteral reflux and secondary hydronephrosis. Urinary involvement is incompletely penetrant, hence "with or without" urinary tract defects.

nodes.description: NFIA is necessary and sufficient to initiate gliogenesis in ventricular-zone progenitors and to maintain inhibition of neurogenesis; reduced NFIA impairs the switch from neurogenesis to gliogenesis and the migration/differentiation of astrocyte precursors that build CNS midline and ependymal structures. The causal links from this cellular defect to the corpus callosum and cerebrospinal fluid phenotypes are inferred from model-organism data (spinal-cord gliogenesis and Nfia-knockout callosal agenesis); direct human midline-glia evidence is limited.
